version.changelog: v5.3.0 — agent mailboxes are open to everyone and live now at $10/mo; request one with POST /v1/mailing-address-requests.

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed mailbox.bot integration for sending and managing postal mail, with real privacy and billing implications that are mostly addressed through sandbox keys, cost caps, and human approval guidance.

dimensions.detail: External API access, bearer keys, document upload, OCR search, and webhook configuration are proportionate to a remote postal-mail service and are disclosed in the artifacts.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The primary OpenClaw and remote MCP setup is straightforward, but README and bridge examples include unpinned npx commands, which is a normal convenience path but weaker than an immutable install reference.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main skill gives clear use cases, key handling guidance, dry-run/cost-cap instructions, and treats mail contents as untrusted; the separate install guide could foreground privacy and physical-mail consequences more prominently.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No local persistence, scheduled tasks, tool replacement, or privilege escalation were found; durable effects are limited to configured remote service state and user-directed physical mail actions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently describe a postal-mail API/MCP integration for outbound mail, inbound mailbox search/OCR, webhooks, and human-approved scan/forward/discard workflows.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent connected to mailbox.bot for real postal-mail workflows. Use sandbox keys first, keep bearer keys out of prompts/logs, set cost caps or require dashboard approval for live sends, and remember that documents, mail metadata, OCR text, webhook data, and mailbox actions are processed by the third-party mailbox.bot service.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The cited DELETE endpoint is a documented cancellation operation for submitted mail, not evidence of unsafe local tool parameter abuse.
[RP1] expected: The unpinned npx install/bridge examples are supply-chain hygiene concerns, but they are disclosed documentation paths and not hidden runtime behavior in the skill artifact.
[E1] expected: The external curl examples access mailbox.bot APIs with an agent key; transmitting documents and mail metadata is inherent to the disclosed remote postal-mail service.
[SQP-2] expected: The privacy-impacting and chargeable operations are real and expected for this skill; SKILL.md and README disclose costs, approvals, sandbox keys, and mail handling, though llms-install.md could state those warnings more prominently.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The server manifest is broad, but SKILL.md contains explicit 'When to use this skill' examples and operating safeguards, reducing unintended invocation risk.
